data.title: Assignments Overdue
data.statement:
On the first day of school after summer vacation, a student realizes he has [[N]] unfinished assignments that are all due today. The student promises to start working on them immediately.

Each assignment [[i]] requires [[Di]] days to complete. For every day an assignment remains overdue, it incurs a daily penalty of [[Pi]] from credits.

The student can only work on one assignment per day and cannot work overtime. Furthermore, once an assignment is started, it must be worked on continuously until finished.

Determine the optimal sequence of assignments to work on, that minimizes the total penalty.

<<Example:>>
Three assignments are due but unfinished.

`           | Needed days | Penalty per
Assignment |  to finish  | overdue day
-----------+-------------+-------------
   1       |      2      |     5
   2       |      1      |    10
   3       |      3      |     2`

The best arrangement is to finish them in this order: 2 1 3

`Today (due date)
  │
  │  ┌────────────────Assignment 2 done. Late for 1 day.  Penalty 10
  │  │     ┌──────────Assignment 1 done. Late for 3 days. Penalty 15
  │  │     │        ┌─Assignment 3 done. Late for 6 days. Penalty 12
  │  │     │        │                                     ──────────
  ▼──▼──┬──▼──┬──┬──▼──┬──┬─                                Total 37
  └──┴──┴──┴──┴──┴──┴──┴──┴─                               (minimum)
             Days`

data.inputDescription:
<<Line 1>>: An integer [[N]], representing the total number of assignments.
<<Next [[N]] lines>>: Each line contains two space-separated integers, [[D]] [[P]].
[[D]] is the number of days needed to complete the assignment, and [[P]] is the penalty cost per overdue day.
data.outputDescription:
• Print a single line containing the optimal sequence of jobs that results in the minimum total penalty.
• Each job must be represented by its 1-indexed position (from 1 to [[N]]) based on the input order.
• The indices should be separated by a single space, with no trailing space at the end of the line.
• If there are more than one sequence that can lead to the same minimal penalty, choose the first one in lexicographic order.

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

On the first day of school after summer vacation, a student realizes he has N unfinished assignments that are all due today. The student promises to start working on them immediately.

Each assignment i requires Di days to complete. For every day an assignment remains overdue, it incurs a daily penalty of Pi from credits.

The student can only work on one assignment per day and cannot work overtime. Furthermore, once an assignment is started, it must be worked on continuously until finished.

Determine the optimal sequence of assignments to work on, that minimizes the total penalty.

Example:
Three assignments are due but unfinished.

           | Needed days | Penalty per
Assignment |  to finish  | overdue day
-----------+-------------+-------------
   1       |      2      |     5
   2       |      1      |    10
   3       |      3      |     2


The best arrangement is to finish them in this order: 2 1 3

Today (due date)
  │
  │  ┌────────────────Assignment 2 done. Late for 1 day.  Penalty 10
  │  │     ┌──────────Assignment 1 done. Late for 3 days. Penalty 15
  │  │     │        ┌─Assignment 3 done. Late for 6 days. Penalty 12
  │  │     │        │                                     ──────────
  ▼──▼──┬──▼──┬──┬──▼──┬──┬─                                Total 37
  └──┴──┴──┴──┴──┴──┴──┴──┴─                               (minimum)
             Days
Input
Line 1: An integer N, representing the total number of assignments.
Next N lines: Each line contains two space-separated integers, D P.
D is the number of days needed to complete the assignment, and P is the penalty cost per overdue day.
Output
• Print a single line containing the optimal sequence of jobs that results in the minimum total penalty.
• Each job must be represented by its 1-indexed position (from 1 to N) based on the input order.
• The indices should be separated by a single space, with no trailing space at the end of the line.
• If there are more than one sequence that can lead to the same minimal penalty, choose the first one in lexicographic order.
Constraints
1 ≤ N ≤ 100
1 ≤ D ≤ 100
0 ≤ P ≤ 1000
Example
Input
3
2 5
1 10
3 2
Output
2 1 3
